licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets map cleanly onto the dominant clusters visible in the data: misrepresentation to obtain a license, fraud/deception during practice, criminal convictions, competence/negligence failures, broad unprofessional/unethical conduct, impairment from substances or health conditions, statutory/regulatory/order violations, reciprocal discipline from other jurisdictions, and a residual catch-all for items like aiding unlicensed practice, patient abuse, fee-splitting, and administrative non-compliance that don't fit the larger groups.

profession_specific.license_type_structu.rationale: These seven buckets capture the primary credential axis (dietitian vs. nutritionist vs. combined), the regulatory mechanism (licensed vs. certified vs. title-only), the sub-professional technician tier, and the provisional/temporary pathway that many states add alongside their full license, covering every item in the distribution without relying on a catch-all.

profession_specific.alternative_credenti.rationale: The items cluster tightly around a handful of specific credentialing bodies (BCNS-CNS, DACBN, ABN/AIN/ASCN membership orgs, CDR/RDN), plus three structurally distinct pathways—an academic degree route, licensure by endorsement from another state, and open-ended departmental qualification—which together cover every item without an oversized catch-all.

profession_specific.protected_titles.rationale: The titles cluster by core role word (dietitian, nutritionist, or the combined form), credential modifier (licensed, registered, certified, provisional), support-level roles (dietetic technician, nutrition therapist/specialist/counselor), and standalone abbreviations/initials that don't carry their full title text.
